text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's Slovenian newspapers:
- Slovenian Christmas tree was placed on St. Peter's Square in the Vatican on Tuesday. Each year the Vatican picks a different country, which donates a Christmas tree.
- The agreement between trade unions and employers determining workers' social benefits should be amended at the latest by the end of May 1997, they said.

- Centre-left Liberal Democrats, Slovenia's biggest party said Sunday's failed referendum on electoral system indicated that parliament itself should decide about needed changes to existing electoral system.

- President Milan Kucan met representatives of Slovenia's three minor parliamentary parties on Tuesday to discuss who should be the next prime minister. Kucan is expected to propose his candidate for prime minister by January 3.
- More than 300 participants took part in the central manifestation marking the 50th anniversary of UNICEF, which was held in Ljubljana on Tuesday.
- Each year more than two million guests, mostly Italians visit one of 10 Slovenian casinos. Turnover of Slovenian casinos every year exceeds 20 billion tolars ($140.8 million).
- President Milan Kucan will start a three-day official visit to Rome and Vatican on Thursday, he will visit his Italian counterpart Oscar Luigi Scalfaro and Pope John Paul.
- The Slovenian Chamber of Economy said on Tuesday 88 percent of apartments in Slovenia are fully owned while only 12 percent are rented. The chamber said that is the best ratio in Europe.
